tagline: Up out of the desert onto an old reef.
intro: NM 137 turns west off US 285 twelve miles north of Carlsbad and climbs out of the Chihuahuan Desert, about 3,000 feet up into the Guadalupe Mountains. The country gets rugged quickly. Prickly pear and sotol grow in patches out of cream-colored limestone, and under it lie wild caves that draw scientists and cavers from all over the world.

These mountains are the back of the old Capitan Reef, built in the Permian at the edge of an inland sea. The byway mapped here covers the first stretch of NM 137, but the highway itself keeps going to the Texas line, where it becomes Dog Canyon Road.

moments.title: Sitting Bull Falls
moments.text: Down County Road 409 lies what the Apache called the hidden gulch, where springs pour over a 200-foot wall of tufa beside stone buildings the CCC put up in 1940.

moments.title: Five Points Vista
moments.text: Well past the end of the mapped stretch, about 50 miles out of Carlsbad on NM 137, an overlook takes in the Rim, a cliff of 1,500 to 2,000 feet along the western edge of the range.

practical: Sitting Bull Falls is a day-use area only, with no camping.
